P-LEAVING.en: You're leaving. What do you say?

FB-GEM.id: Permata ini masuk ke Kotak Permata Anda.
FB-GEM.en: This gem goes into your Gem box.

body.id: 10 vokal dasar: garis panjangnya berdiri │ atau berbaring ─. Garis pendek kedua menambah bunyi y.
body.en: 10 basic vowels: the long line stands │ or lies ─. A second short stroke adds a y sound.

body.id: Suku kata yang diawali vokal memakai ㅇ yang tidak berbunyi: ㅏ → 아 (a), ㅗ → 오 (o).
body.en: A syllable that starts with a vowel takes a silent ㅇ: ㅏ → 아 (a), ㅗ → 오 (o).

body.id: Salam aman untuk siapa saja: 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo). Terima kasih: 감사합니다 (gamsahamnida).
body.en: A safe hello for anyone: 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo). Thank you: 감사합니다 (gamsahamnida).

body.id: Konsonan di kiri vokal berdiri (나 na) atau di atas vokal berbaring (노 no).
body.en: A consonant goes left of a standing vowel (나 na) or above a lying one (노 no).

body.id: Angka asli 하나, 둘, 셋 (hana, dul, set) untuk menghitung benda dan umur.
body.en: Native numbers 하나, 둘, 셋 (hana, dul, set) count things and age.

body.id: Angka Sino 일, 이, 삼 (il, i, sam) untuk uang, tanggal, dan telepon; 0 dibaca 공 (gong).
body.en: Sino-Korean 일, 이, 삼 (il, i, sam) are for money, dates and phones; 0 is read 공 (gong).

body.id: Satu blok = satu suku kata. Huruf ketiga di bawah: 받침 (batchim), seperti ㅂ di 집 (jip).
body.en: One block = one syllable. A third letter at the bottom is a 받침 (batchim): ㅂ in 집 (jip).

body.id: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ berhembus; ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ tegang: 달 (dal), 탈 (tal), 딸 (ttal).
body.en: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ have a puff; ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are tight: 달 (dal), 탈 (tal), 딸 (ttal).

body.id: 받침 bisa berubah bunyi: 옷 (ot, baju) ditulis dengan ㅅ, tetapi dibaca t.
body.en: A 받침 can change its sound: 옷 (ot, clothes) is spelled with ㅅ but read t.

body.id: Sopan: 어머니 (eomeoni) ibu, 아버지 (abeoji) ayah. Akrab: 엄마 (eomma), 아빠 (appa).
body.en: Polite: 어머니 (eomeoni) mother, 아버지 (abeoji) father. Casual: 엄마 (eomma), 아빠 (appa).

body.id: Kakak: perempuan bilang 언니 (eonni), 오빠 (oppa); laki-laki bilang 누나 (nuna), 형 (hyeong).
body.en: Older siblings: women say 언니 (eonni), 오빠 (oppa); men say 누나 (nuna), 형 (hyeong).

body.id: Perkenalan: 저는 인도네시아 사람이에요 (jeoneun indonesia saramieyo), saya orang Indonesia.
body.en: Introducing yourself: 저는 인도네시아 사람이에요 (jeoneun indonesia saramieyo), I'm Indonesian.

body.id: Pesan dengan: benda + 주세요 (juseyo). 커피 하나 주세요 (keopi hana juseyo) = satu kopi, ya.
body.en: Order with: item + 주세요 (juseyo). 커피 하나 주세요 (keopi hana juseyo) = one coffee, please.

body.id: Tanya harga: 얼마예요? (eolmayeyo?) Minta tagihan: 계산해 주세요 (gyesanhae juseyo).
body.en: Ask the price: 얼마예요? (eolmayeyo?) Ask for the bill: 계산해 주세요 (gyesanhae juseyo).

body.id: Sebelum makan: 잘 먹겠습니다 (jal meokgetseumnida), kira-kira "selamat makan".
body.en: Before eating: 잘 먹겠습니다 (jal meokgetseumnida), roughly "I'll enjoy this meal".

body.id: Tanya tempat: ___ 어디예요? (eodiyeyo?) Contoh: 화장실 어디예요? (hwajangsil eodiyeyo?)
body.en: Ask where: ___ 어디예요? (eodiyeyo?) For example: 화장실 어디예요? (hwajangsil eodiyeyo?)

body.id: Jawabannya: 여기 (yeogi) di sini, 저기 (jeogi) di sana. Memanggil orang: 저기요 (jeogiyo)!
body.en: Answers: 여기 (yeogi) here, 저기 (jeogi) over there. To get attention: 저기요 (jeogiyo)!

body.id: Di taksi, tunjukkan alamat dan bilang 여기로 가 주세요 (yeogiro ga juseyo).
body.en: In a taxi, show the address and say 여기로 가 주세요 (yeogiro ga juseyo).

items.source: Hunminjeongeum Haerye (1446), postface by Jeong In-ji: a wise man can learn the letters before the morning is over, a slow one within ten days; UNESCO Memory of the World Register, 'Hunminjeongum Manuscript' (inscribed 1997); Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Hangul'.

model_answer.id: Hangul diumumkan tahun 1446 dalam naskah Hunminjeongeum, "bunyi yang benar untuk mengajar rakyat". Penutupnya berkata: orang cerdas menguasainya sebelum pagi usai, yang lambat dalam sepuluh hari.
model_answer.en: Hangul was proclaimed in 1446 in Hunminjeongeum, "the correct sounds for instructing the people". Its afterword says a clever person learns it before the morning is over, a slow one within ten days.

items.source: Hunminjeongeum Haerye (1446), chapter Jejahae ('Explanation of the design of the letters'): ㄱ ㄴ ㅁ ㅅ ㅇ modelled on the tongue, mouth, teeth and throat; vowels built from heaven (·), earth (ㅡ) and human (ㅣ); Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Hangul'; National Institute of Korean Language (korean.go.kr).

model_answer.id: Hunminjeongeum menjelaskan desainnya: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㅁ, ㅅ, ㅇ meniru lidah, mulut, gigi, dan tenggorokan. Vokal dibangun dari tiga unsur: titik (langit), ㅡ (bumi), dan ㅣ (manusia).
model_answer.en: Hunminjeongeum explains its design: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㅁ, ㅅ and ㅇ copy the tongue, mouth, teeth and throat. Vowels are built from three parts: a dot (heaven), ㅡ (earth) and ㅣ (human).

model_answer.id: Sejak 2009, sebagian murid di Kota Baubau, Sulawesi Tenggara, belajar menulis bahasa Cia-Cia dengan hangul. Hangul bukan aksara resmi di sana, tetapi bunyi bahasa daerah kita pun muat dalam blok hangul.

model_answer.id: Panggil dulu (저기요), tanya tempatnya, dengar jawabannya, lalu berterima kasih.
model_answer.en: First get attention (저기요), ask where, hear the answer, then say thanks.
